parsed.thesis: 无终止逻辑的重复行为是将失败外包给外部纠正：任何迭代或等待动作在开始前必须自带停止条件，在每次迭代中依据可观察状态验证是否满足，且一旦观察到完成信号或收到明确禁止指令，必须立即停止并转变计划，而非等待系统级纠正来打断。

principleCandidate.title: Termination-Aware Repetition: pre-declare exit conditions and verify observed state each iteration
principleCandidate.rationale: 根因是开放式等待循环缺乏内在终止逻辑：重复调用在目标状态已被观察到之后仍继续，甚至忽视明确的禁止指令，直到外部严重纠正才停下。Dreamer 的五个候选共同指向一个结构性修复——进入循环前声明退出条件（护栏前置）、每次迭代后观察并与目标比较（执行即验证）、以可观察完成信号与显式指令为硬停止条件。将终止逻辑内建于重复动作本身，可从结构上阻止冗余调用，而非依赖迟到的外部反馈。
principleCandidate.scope: 适用于任何随时间重复的行为：等待/轮询循环、重试、重复工具调用、周期性检查。尤其在上下文中已存在完成信号、配额上限或明确停止指令的场合；不限于具体的 sessions_yield 场景。

risks: 与核心公理存在部分重叠：本原则实质上是 T-05（护栏前置）、T-07（行动后观察验证）、T-03（以可观察证据为依据）与 T-02（显式指令优先）在循环控制场景下的合成应用，若被采纳需明确其为场景化细化而非新增基础公理，避免公理体系冗余。
对完成信号的误读可能导致过早终止：例如将单个子代理的 settle 信号误认为全部完成，从而提前退出等待并收集到不完整的结果。
预声明的最大迭代/等待上限难以校准：上限过低会截断必要的等待，过高则重新引入资源浪费，需要结合实际任务时延动态调整。
将任何显式指令一律视为硬停止可能被滥用：若指令来源不可信或与更高优先级目标冲突，机械停止可能中断正当流程，需保留对指令层级与来源的判断。

principleDraft.title: Termination-Aware Repetition: pre-declare exit conditions and verify observed state each iteration
principleDraft.statement: 任何迭代、等待、轮询或重试动作在开始前必须声明明确的退出条件——以可观察状态表述的完成判据、最大迭代次数或时长上限、以及"收到显式停止/禁止指令即停"；每次迭代后必须将观察到的状态与这些退出条件比对，一旦满足完成判据或收到显式停止指令，立即停止重复并转入下一步计划；绝不允许重复行为依赖外部系统纠正（如配额耗尽或强制中断）来充当事实上的终止机制。
principleDraft.rationale: 根因诊断表明：开放式等待/轮询循环缺乏内建的终止逻辑，重复调用在目标状态已被观察到之后仍然继续，甚至忽视上下文中已存在的显式停止指令，直到外部严重纠正（配额耗尽、系统强制中断）才停止——这等于把"何时停止"的判断外包给外部系统。将终止逻辑前置（进入循环前声明退出条件）、每轮执行即验证（迭代后与目标状态比对）、以可观察完成信号与显式指令为硬停止条件，可从结构上阻断冗余重复，而非依赖迟到的外部反馈。
applicability: 等待/轮询循环：等待子任务、子代理或外部系统进入目标状态（如 sessions_yield 式的 settle 等待）
重试逻辑：对可能失败的操作进行有限次重试
重复工具调用：同一工具或等价操作的连续多次调用
周期性检查：按时间间隔反复探测系统状态
上下文中已存在完成信号、配额上限或显式停止指令的任何重复行为场景
antiPatterns: 无退出条件的开放式循环：进入重复前未声明完成判据或迭代/时长上限
目标状态已被观察到之后仍继续迭代
在重复过程中收到显式停止/禁止指令后仍继续调用
把外部系统纠正（配额耗尽、强制中断、人工打断）当作事实上的终止机制
每轮迭代后不做状态比对，仅机械重复固定次数
观察到完成信号后不转变计划，而是反复检查已确认完成的状态

intentContract.ownerIntent: Owner 希望代理的任何重复等待/轮询/重试行为都自带终止逻辑——一旦观察到完成状态或收到明确停止指令就立即自行停止并转变计划，而不是耗尽资源直到系统级纠正被迫打断。
intentContract.targetBehavior: 代理在进入任何重复动作前，先声明退出条件（可观察的完成判据 + 最大迭代/时长上限 + 显式停止指令即停）；每轮迭代后检查观察到的状态是否满足退出条件；满足或收到停止指令时立即退出循环并转入下一步计划。审查者在工具轨迹中应能看到：循环前的退出条件声明、每轮迭代后的状态检查动作、以及条件满足后的及时退出。
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: 重复调用在目标状态已被观察到之后仍继续；在收到显式停止/禁止指令后仍继续调用；以无退出条件的开放式循环运行，直至配额耗尽或系统强制纠正才终止。
intentContract.evidenceSource: 痛点诊断：一个无终止逻辑的等待/轮询循环（sessions_yield 场景）在完成信号已可观察、显式停止指令已存在的情况下仍持续重复调用，最终由外部系统级纠正打断并造成资源浪费。
intentContract.validationExpectation: 评估者应要求任何由本原则生成的规则同时具备三个可检验要件： 循环进入前的退出条件声明（完成判据与上限）； 每轮迭代后对可观察状态的比对； 观察到完成信号或收到显式停止指令时立即停止并转变计划。缺少任一要件、或允许在已观察到完成信号后继续迭代的规则，均判定为对意图不忠实。

risks: 与核心公理存在重叠：本原则实质上是 T-05（护栏前置）、T-07（行动后观察验证）、T-03（以可观察证据为依据）与 T-02（显式指令优先）在循环控制场景下的合成细化；若被采纳应标注为场景化细化而非新增基础公理，避免公理体系冗余。
完成信号误读可能导致过早终止：例如把单个子代理的 settle 信号当作全部完成，提前退出等待并收集到不完整的结果。
预声明的最大迭代/等待上限难以校准：上限过低会截断必要的等待，过高则重新引入资源浪费，需要结合任务实际时延动态调整。
将任何显式指令一律视为硬停止可能被滥用：若指令来源不可信或与更高优先级目标冲突，机械停止可能中断正当流程，需保留对指令层级与来源的判断。
原则可能被过度泛化到非重复的单次动作，导致无谓的前置声明开销；规则生成时应限定于重复性行为。

principleDraft.title: Termination-Aware Repetition: pre-declare exit conditions and verify observed state each iteration
principleDraft.statement: Any iterative or waiting action must carry its own termination logic: before entering a repetition (wait/poll loop, retry, repeated tool call), declare explicit exit conditions tied to observable state; after each iteration, compare the observed state against those conditions; and stop immediately and switch to the next planned step as soon as the target state is observed in context or an explicit stop/prohibition instruction is received. Repetition must never persist after its completion condition is already observable, and must never depend on external system correction to be interrupted.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is an open-ended wait loop with no internal termination logic: after signal_collector had already reported 'all subagents settled' and explicitly instructed not to call sessions_yield again, the assistant kept issuing the same wait call until a severe external correction interrupted it. Embedding termination into the repetition itself — pre-declared exit conditions before the loop, per-iteration observation compared against the target state, and hard stops on observed completion signals and explicit directives — structurally blocks redundant calls at the source instead of relying on late external feedback.
applicability: Wait/poll loops that yield until a target state is reached (e.g., sessions_yield waiting for subagents to settle)
Retry loops and repeated identical tool calls
Periodic checks or monitoring actions repeated over time
Any repetition performed when the context already contains a completion signal, a quota/limit notice, or an explicit stop or prohibition instruction
antiPatterns: Continuing to call a wait/yield tool (e.g., sessions_yield) after an observable completion signal such as 'all subagents settled' is already in context
Re-issuing a call pattern after receiving an explicit instruction to stop or not to make that call
Entering a wait/retry loop without declaring any exit condition or bound
Repeating a call without comparing the latest observable output against the target state between iterations
Treating system-level severe correction as the normal mechanism that ends a loop

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants the agent to stop a wait/repetition pattern on its own as soon as the context shows the awaited state is reached (e.g., 'all subagents settled') or an explicit stop instruction exists — never continuing redundant calls like sessions_yield until a severe external correction fires.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Before each repeated or waiting call, the agent scans context for completion signals and its pre-declared exit condition; upon observing the target state or a stop directive, it terminates the loop immediately and moves to the successor step (e.g., collecting subagent results), so the trajectory shows zero identical wait calls after the completion signal appears.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Open-ended repetition that ignores already-observable completion state or explicit prohibition instructions — continuing or re-issuing the same wait/repeated call and stopping only when an external system correction interrupts.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Pain pain_host_620a1683e2eeb7a714ce5eb67aac55b08dc8bee7164211358c5f00f308068791: after signal_collector reported all subagents settled and instructed 'do not wait or call sessions_yield again', the assistant repeated sessions_yield anyway; the severe user correction was auto-detected by the after_tool_call hook (diagnosis_pain_host_620a1683e2eeb7a714ce5eb67aac55b08dc8bee7164211358c5f00f308068791).
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should verify that derived rules (a) block or warn on a repeated wait/yield call when a completion signal or explicit stop instruction already exists in context, (b) require the exit condition to be checked against observable state on every iteration rather than relying only on a fixed iteration cap, and (c) direct the agent to the successor step such as result collection; a compliant trajectory terminates the loop on the observed signal with no subsequent identical calls and no system correction.

risks: Overlaps core axioms: this principle is a loop-control synthesis of T-03 (observable evidence), T-05 (guardrails before execution), T-07 (observe and compare after acting) and T-02 (explicit directives override habits); it should be adopted as a scenario-specific refinement, not a new base axiom, to avoid axiom-set redundancy.
Misreading a partial completion signal (e.g., a single subagent's settle) as full completion can terminate the loop prematurely and collect incomplete results.
Pre-declared maximum iteration/wait bounds are hard to calibrate: too low truncates necessary waiting, too high re-introduces wasted calls.

Treating any explicit instruction as an unconditional hard stop can be abused when the instruction source is untrusted or conflicts with higher-priority owner goals; instruction provenance and hierarchy still require judgment.

principleDraft.statement: Every repetition of a waiting, polling, or retry action must be gated on a fresh check: before each repeat, compare the latest observable state against the loop's termination goal, and if the goal is already met — or an explicit system/owner stop signal is present in context — terminate the loop immediately and proceed to the next phase. A repeated action is justified only while its preconditions still hold.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is a waiting loop with no internal exit basis: repetition was driven by procedural habit (keep calling sessions_yield) rather than by comparing fresh observable state against the termination goal, so the loop stopped only when the system issued a severe external correction. Embedding the termination check as a precondition of each repetition intercepts the redundant call before execution and restores self-termination, which is more fundamental than after-the-fact correction and avoids both wasted calls and eroded system trust.
applicability: Orchestration wait loops for subagent/subtask completion (e.g., sessions_yield while subagents run)
Polling loops on external system state with a defined success condition
Retry loops where a prior identical call already succeeded or the blocking condition has disappeared
Habitual repeated steps about to be re-executed while environment state may have changed since the last decision
Repetition that is contradicted by an explicit system or owner stop instruction in context
antiPatterns: Calling sessions_yield (or an equivalent wait/poll call) after a signal_collector report that all subagents have settled and instructed not to wait further
Continuing a loop because it is 'the next step in the flow' without re-verifying that the exit condition is still unmet
Treating an explicit 'stop waiting / do not call this again' message as ignorable background noise while continuing habitual behavior
Letting external system correction be the only mechanism that ends a repeated action

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants repeated wait/poll calls (like sessions_yield) to stop as soon as observable state shows the awaited condition is satisfied or an explicit stop instruction is given, rather than persisting until the system forcibly corrects the agent.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Before each repeated wait/poll call, the agent's tool trajectory shows it consulted the latest state and signals in context; when a settled/complete signal (e.g., 'all subagents settled') or an explicit stop instruction exists, it issues no further wait call and visibly proceeds to the next phase such as result collection.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Repeating sessions_yield-style wait/poll calls while the context already contains evidence that all awaited subagents have settled or an explicit instruction to stop waiting — a loop that terminates only through external system correction.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Severe user-correction pain (pain_host_620a1683e2eeb7a714ce5eb67aac55b08dc8bee7164211358c5f00f308068791) detected by the after_tool_call hook: the assistant kept calling sessions_yield after signal_collector reported all subagents settled with an explicit 'do not wait or call sessions_yield again' message; the diagnosis cites ignored observable state (T-03) and missing internal loop termination (T-07).
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a derived rule only if it triggers precisely when a termination signal (e.g., 'all subagents settled') or an explicit stop instruction is already present in context AND the agent is about to repeat the wait call; compliant traces must show a state check before each repetition and immediate exit afterward, and any rule change that permits repeating the wait despite such signals must be flagged as contradicting this intent.

risks: Overlaps core axioms T-03, T-07 and T-05: this principle is a loop-control specialization (pre-repetition gate plus stop-signal compliance), and downstream adoption must treat it as a specialization rather than duplicate rule construction

Premature exit: a 'settled' signal that is stale, partial, or from an unreliable source could cause abandoning a still-needed wait; derived rules should require the signal to be explicit and current (e.g., naming the awaited entities)
Over-triggering: a naively generated rule could block legitimate waits while subagents are still running; trigger conditions must distinguish 'all settled' from 'some still running'
Per-repetition state checks add overhead in fast polling loops; check granularity may need bounding in performance-sensitive contexts

Hardcoding termination on a single signal risks misjudgment in more complex state models (partial completion, staged results); the principle should be applied together with a sufficient system state model (T-01)

principleDraft.title: Gate Every Repeated Action on Fresh State and Explicit Stop Signals
principleDraft.statement: Before each repetition of any wait, poll, retry, or recurring orchestration step, re-read the latest observable state and compare it against the loop's termination goal; if that goal is already satisfied (e.g., every awaited subagent has settled) or an explicit stop signal has been received, terminate the repetition immediately instead of executing the action again by habit or fixed schedule. Every repetitive behavior must carry its own internal exit criterion and must never depend on external correction to stop.
principleDraft.rationale: The root cause of the observed pain is that the wait loop lacked a built-in exit basis: repetition was driven by procedural inertia rather than by a fresh comparison of observable state against the termination goal. Embedding a pre-repetition gate — fresh state check plus obedience to explicit stop signals — intercepts redundant actions (such as repeated sessions_yield after all subagents settled) before execution, giving the behavior self-terminating capacity. This is a more fundamental fix than post-hoc external correction, which both wastes resources and erodes system trust.
applicability: Wait loops checking whether subagents or subtasks have completed within an orchestration flow
Polling external system state such as APIs, background jobs, or resource availability
Retry loops whose termination depends on a condition rather than a fixed count
Fixed recurring steps in an orchestration where the environment state may have changed since the previous decision
Any moment the agent is about to repeat an action it has already performed, especially when an explicit stop or cancel signal may arrive mid-loop
antiPatterns: Repeating a previously executed action (e.g., sessions_yield) on habit or fixed schedule without first checking whether the awaited condition is already satisfied
Continuing a polling or wait loop after an explicit stop or cancel signal has been received
Basing loop termination on a stale or cached state snapshot instead of freshly observed state
Persisting in a loop until the host or system externally corrects it, rather than exiting via an internal state-versus-goal check
Treating a single possibly stale or partial 'settled' signal as sufficient termination without validating its freshness and completeness

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants the agent to stop repeating actions that have already become pointless — such as issuing redundant sessions_yield calls after all awaited subagents have settled — on its own initiative, without the host or system having to externally correct the loop.
intentContract.targetBehavior: In any wait, poll, retry, or repeat loop, the agent's tool trajectory shows a fresh state query or condition check immediately before each repeated action, and the loop exits as soon as the termination goal is verified met or an explicit stop signal arrives.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Repeating a prior action purely by habit or fixed schedule while the latest observable state already satisfies the termination goal, or continuing to repeat after an explicit stop signal, such that only external intervention ends the loop.
intentContract.evidenceSource: The diagnosed pain of the agent continuing to issue redundant sessions_yield calls after all awaited subagents had settled, requiring host-level correction to stop the repetition.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should require that any rule derived from this principle mandates a pre-repetition fresh-state check against the termination goal and immediate obedience to explicit stop signals, verifiable in the sessions_yield wait-loop scenario and analogous polling or retry contexts; a rule that permits repeating an action without a fresh state check, or that allows ignoring a stop signal, contradicts this intent and must be flagged.

risks: Partial overlap with core axioms T-07 (observe result after acting and compare with intent) and T-03 (use observable evidence before inferring): this principle is their pre-action specialization for loop control; adoption must frame it as a refinement, not duplicate rule construction

Early-exit risk: if a 'settled' or terminal signal is stale, partial, or from an unreliable source, treating it as a termination condition may abandon necessary waiting before work is truly complete; rule generation should require validating signal freshness and completeness
High-frequency state checks can add overhead to fast, tight loops; in performance-sensitive contexts the check granularity must be balanced rather than maximally frequent
Hardcoding a single terminal signal risks misjudging complex state models (partial completion, staged results); the principle should be applied jointly with sufficient system modeling per T-01
Scope creep risk: applying the principle to one-shot (non-repeated) actions would dilute its meaning; it must be scoped strictly to repeated, polled, or looped behavior

Convergence must be self-detected: declare the observable completion condition before entering a loop, and re-ground each iteration's decision in the latest state signals rather than the originally planned sequence.

principleDraft.title: Anchor repetitive loops to self-detected termination on observed completion signals
principleDraft.statement: Any repetitive or iterative action must carry its own termination: before entering a wait/poll/retry/monitor loop, declare the observable completion condition, and before each subsequent iteration, re-check the latest state signals against it; as soon as the latest observable evidence shows the awaited condition is met (e.g., a signal that all subagents have settled), stop the loop immediately and proceed to the next phase instead of continuing until an external correction intervenes.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is a wait loop whose continuation was driven by the originally planned sequence rather than the observed goal state: the assistant kept calling sessions_yield after signal_collector had already reported all subagents settled, stopping only under a severe external correction. Making continuation contingent on an explicit termination predicate re-checked against the latest evidence makes convergence self-detected, eliminating idle repetition, wasted calls, and dependence on external intervention. This is a specialization of T-03 and T-07 to iterative loops, not a replacement for them.
applicability: Multi-agent coordination waits, e.g., polling/yielding while subagents run before collecting their results
Polling or monitoring loops that wait for a state change or completion signal observable between iterations
Retry loops whose success or terminal failure is observable between attempts
Open-ended waits where a signal collector or system message reports the awaited condition
antiPatterns: Issuing the same wait/poll call (e.g., sessions_yield) again after an in-context signal has already reported the awaited condition met, such as 'all subagents settled, do not wait'
Running a loop with no internal termination predicate, relying on external system correction to stop it
Deciding each iteration from the originally planned sequence while ignoring newer state messages returned since entering the loop
Treating a wait-for-completion step as a fixed procedural stage that runs to exhaustion regardless of observed completion

intentContract.ownerIntent: The owner wants the agent to stop repetitive waiting/polling on its own the moment observable state shows the awaited condition is met (such as 'all subagents settled'), rather than repeating the call until a severe external correction forces it to stop.
intentContract.targetBehavior: In the tool trajectory, no wait/poll call (e.g., sessions_yield) appears after a completion signal for the awaited condition is already present in context; instead the agent visibly checks the latest signal, recognizes the condition as met, and transitions to the next phase (e.g., result collection).
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Continuing to issue repeated wait/poll calls after an explicit completion signal ('all subagents settled, stop waiting') has already been observed — a repetition loop with no internal termination that persists until external correction.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Severe user-correction pain pain_host_620a1683e2eeb7a714ce5eb67aac55b08dc8bee7164211358c5f00f308068791: the after_tool_call hook caught the assistant calling sessions_yield after signal_collector reported all subagents settled and instructed it to stop waiting; the diagnosis attributes this to ignoring observable state (T-03) and missing post-action verification (T-07), and all four Dreamer candidates converge on evidence-based, self-detected loop termination.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should require that any rule generated from this principle fires on a repeated wait/poll call issued after an in-context completion signal (e.g., sessions_yield following 'all subagents settled'), while permitting waits for which no completion evidence exists yet; rules that block legitimate waiting without a completion signal, or force exit on ambiguous or partial signals, contradict this intent and must be flagged rather than merged.

risks: Closely overlaps core axioms T-03 (act on observable evidence) and T-07 (verify outcomes against intent): this principle is their specialization to repetitive loops, so downstream rules must target loop termination specifically to avoid duplicating existing axiom coverage

A loosely defined termination predicate can trigger premature exit on false-positive completion signals (misreading partial or stale signals as full completion), stopping work before the goal is truly achieved
Mandating a declared predicate for every trivial fixed-step loop adds ceremony that conflicts with T-06 (simplest intervention); scope should stay on open-ended or discretionary repetition
Re-reading and re-evaluating all context signals on every iteration of high-frequency loops may consume excessive attention; the per-iteration check should be limited to completion-relevant signals
